inputs.typed_scope_note: The current signatures are pinned to the exact metric object. The source polyhedral subgroup is defined locally as finite integer sums of actual lifted spherical simplex integration objects, including support covers under addition and cancellation. Integration support locality and Stokes are standard external laws, with no own deformation/approximation/transfer conclusion. Neighborhood pushforward is on the actual supported-current subgroup, with exact boundary commutation, support image and standard individual L^k mass law. Euclidean area calculus supplies only the canonical metric Jacobian, standard area inequality and generic smooth round-lift locality; no incident envelope or own sharp upper estimate is a field. The two-stage pushforward signature states only the generic canonical composition/identity/equality-on-support law for any two neighborhood maps whose composition is the identity on the current support. It has no spherical geometry, approximation, deformation, sharp mass or filling field; the actual inverse realization and retraction identity are local proofs. Actual Lipschitz singular simplex integration has only the canonical objects, support in the actual parameterized image and standard alternating-face Stokes. The corresponding integration chain map is constructed locally from the free abelian groups and native alternating face boundary. Canonical affine/Lipschitz-simplex integration compatibility states only that the pushforward of an actual affine simplex integration is the integration of its actual composed Lipschitz parameterization for any neighborhood map. Its compact-domain Lipschitz parameterization and the explicit normalized-affine spherical formula are local proofs; no polyhedral preservation, approximation or mass estimate is supplied. Additional generic locality facts say zero mass is the zero current, and any rectifiable current supported in an affine space has approximate tangent inside its direction space a.e. They contain no projective or spherical rank assertion. The collapsed-projective rank drop and Gram/exterior-Jacobian vanishing are local proofs, then the standard area law yields zero pushed current. Generic Euclidean simplex separation is an explicit real-valued test-evaluation corollary: for each actual strict simplex in a finite Euclidean complex, a compactly supported smooth test form in a small ball around its relative interior avoids every other simplex of the same dimension; canonical affine integration and normalization give evaluation 1 on that simplex and 0 on the others. Only these real additive evaluations are supplied; injectivity of finite integer simplicial integration, its spherical pull-push version, and the deduction that a closed integrated current has a closed simplicial representative are native proofs. This elementary corollary is based on standard test-form locality and Euclidean compatibility, not stated as a separate numbered theorem in the cited sources. On a finite clopen partition, ComponentCurrentDecompositionInput supplies only the standard canonical inclusion pushforwards of the actual subtype inclusions, additive current restrictions commuting with boundary, exact reconstruction, mass additivity for currents with disjoint component supports, and the same-component/other-component restriction identities. Native finite sums then assemble cycles, homologies, prescribed fillings and mass limits; no approximation or own joint transfer bound is a field. CompactCurrentHomotopyInput supplies the actual canonical interval-product homotopy push operator for arbitrary Lipschitz H:[0,1]×K→X and its standard boundary formula with actual canonical endpoint pushforwards. LocalCurrentPushforwardCalculusInput supplies only generic identity-on-current-support locality and the individual local L^k mass law when a common local Lipschitz constant L holds near every support point. Neither field asserts any deformation, carrier, relative fixing, approximation, prescribed filling or joint transfer conclusion. These are applied to the already natively constructed actual relative homotopy and map.
